section: Introduction
focus: Real-world impact of the literature-database gap in rare disease: evidence that disease-causing variants and patient-level phenotypes published in case reports are missing from ClinVar or other databases, and the cost of diagnostic delay (published before 2026-11).
context: Hook: Rare-disease genotype-phenotype knowledge is fragmented: variants sit in ClinVar and OMIM, phenotype vocabulary in HPO, a small share of cases in phenopacket-store, and most individual patients only in published case reports, so a laboratory querying ClinVar cannot see a causative variant that was published but never submitted (idea.md Problem). Use the corrected Alexander disease figures as the concrete hook: about 550 published patients and 182 causative variants (2024 meta-analysis) against 76 ClinVar P/LP records (release 2026-10-12) and 13 OMIM allelic variants (gene entry frozen 2026-10-28) (log §1.11; never the application's 72 / ~12). None of the twelve genes has a folder in phenopacket-store (735 gene folders at commit ca133e6, 2026-11-04; log §1.2). Diseases recur faster than hand curation, so the need is a pipeline that can be pointed at any disease with provenance a clinician can check.. Gap: Prior LLM and text-mining work extracts variants or HPO terms, but rarely (i) attaches a verbatim, machine-checked quote to every value with 'not reported' as a first-class output, (ii) evaluates against reference databases kept strictly out of extraction, and (iii) separates a model's self-check from a human-measured error rate. Scope the gap strictly to what this report evaluates: a frozen, pre-registered pipeline run on six registered rare diseases (plus five extension diseases and one exploratory disease reported apart), with automatic concordance against ClinVar/OMIM and gap candidates; its human-measured accuracy (O1, the primary outcome) is pending, written as \HR{o1_unsupported_n} of 250. The introduction must say early, in a short status paragraph, that every human result is a boxed placeholder to be filled by script, that the two pre-freeze pilot audits were above the 2% target (6.0%, 3/50; 6.3%, 3/48), and that this is version 4 of an internal interim report superseding versions 2 (2026-10-28) and 3 (2026-11-02). End with contributions exactly as idea.md 'Contributions' states them (pipeline under a frozen pre-registration on twelve diseases; database-held-out evaluation with dossiers ready for adjudication; an honest account of what is not yet known). Do not claim accuracy, submissions, or that pilot results generalize; do not mention the SLIDERS ablation.

section: Related Work: 2.1 Variant and phenotype extraction from the biomedical literature
focus: large language model extraction of HGVS variants and HPO phenotypes from full-text case reports evaluated against ClinVar
context: Mission: Find how these systems are evaluated (corpus type: case reports vs clinical notes vs abstracts; per-value provenance; negation/absence handling; comparison to curated databases) and what accuracies they report, up to 2026-11. Do not look for new competitors to benchmark; the only model comparison in the log is Claude vs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash under an identical scaffold.. Hypothesis: Most systems output entities or variant-paper links without a verbatim quote per value, collapse 'not reported' into absence, work on abstracts or clinical notes rather than full-text case reports, and score against annotations rather than held-out databases; LLM numeric/count fields are error-prone.

section: 3. Methodology - 3.2 Extraction with provenance and three-state phenotypes
focus: research paper or technical report introducing the 'Claude' family of large language models (Anthropic), including 'Claude Opus'
context: Must-have citation for section covering: The SLIDERS method (evidence tables with verbatim excerpts as provenance, code-writing reconciliation) run as a home-built version with Claude Code helper agents on the funded claude.ai account, not the public SLIDERS code (D-20, log §1.1, §1.6); credit SLIDERS and the Lam lab. One Claude Opus helper per paper reads only its paper, the instruction file, the schema and the rules file; no web access; told not to use anything it remembers about the paper. Served model claude-opus-5-5 (registered manifests recorded the alias 'opus'; served_model added 2026-10-28, marked). No sampling parameters on this route; training cutoff June 2026 (log §1.6). Four pinned files frozen 2026-10-20 (extract_v6, gatekeeper_v4, schema_ha20_v5 with five tables, extraction_rules_v1); per-disease instantiation swaps 12 lines and a 20-item checklist written from open guidelines/reviews with every quote checked (D-38; log §1.5). Record rules: every value carries PMID + verbatim quote; deterministic span check on all values; 'not reported' is first-class and has no quote; normal findings recorded as excluded abnormality (D-27); variant fields only from statements about this person (D-29); no positional reading of stacked cells (D-31) (log §1.7). State the known frozen gap: extraction v6 has no hedge rule, so hedged statuses are dropped by the gatekeeper and end as not reported (D-36; smoke run 5 of 23 unsupported were hedged).

section: 3. Methodology - 3.6 Human assessment design (D-55)
focus: Cohen (A Coefficient of Agreement for Nominal Scales)
context: Must-have citation for section covering: Refer to Figure fig_human_assessment. Accepted by the PI 2026-11-15: volunteer raters in rotating groups with a calibration round and a floor, replacing two fixed raters and a tie-breaker; nine raters from 2026-11-16, two of them members of the adjudication panel; no rater named (log §3 D-55, §4). Calibration set: 99 candidate claims from registered runs outside the O1 sample, labelled by the PI blind to the gatekeeper (64 supported, 29 unsupported, 5 cannot verify, 1 quote not in paper; sittings 60 in 59.6 min, 15 in 17.2 min, 24 in 16.3 min). Set rule fixed before any label; two amendments after his labels and before any rater saw anything (one kind of claim capped on the unsupported side; repeated paper+quote skipped). Do NOT name the capped kind or the cap. Final 40 claims (20/20) from 39 papers; 35 shared by all three versions (log §4.1). How a rating counts and the floor (>=15 of 20 unsupported caught and >=18 of 20 supported passed; fixed before any result); what 20 unsupported claims can resolve (20/20 -> 83%-100%; 16/20 -> 56%-94%) (log §4.1). Main assessment: every audit claim read by 3 raters in seeded groups of three (84 groups with nine raters), named registered pair + tie-breaker, rule C unchanged; kappa per pair on shared claims; triage 2 raters + PI; adjudication 2 + third on disagreement; nothing goes to submission without panel approval and PI sign-off; registered, extension and Majeed studies scored separately (log §4.2). Plan A vs Plan B in one sentence with Plan A 250/50/214 and Plan B 527/146/269 and hours per rater for nine raters (19.1 vs 25.7; planning figures, not measurements; adjudication time assumed); full table in Appendix F. Signpost: calibration results appear in Section 4.10 and Table (pending results) as \HR{cal_raters_finished} etc. Reference labels compared with the gatekeeper (34 of 65 removed claims labelled supported; 3 of 34 kept labelled unsupported) belong in Section 4.2, stated as not error rates.
